rename.to: Cannot get final name for export "default" in "delegated ..." with Webpack 3 scope hoisting

body: I encountered a similar issue. Like the error suggests I am using a DLL lib and wonder if there is an incompatibility with the DLL plugin and the scope hoisting plugin
seems to be an incompatibility between DLL plugin and the concat plugin. bundles just fine when not using DLL reference plugin.

> seems to be an incompatibility between DLL plugin and the concat plugin. bundles just fine when not using DLL reference plugin.

yep

I got a very similar error after enabling the scope hoisting plugin:

```
ERROR in chunk main [initial]
[name].bundle.js
Cannot get final name for export "platformBrowserDynamic" in "delegated ./node_modules/@angular/platform-browser-dynamic/@angular/platform-browser-dynamic.es5.js from dll-reference vendor_lib" (known exports: true, known reexports: )
```
When using webpack3.0 with DLL plugin, the error accured.
Are there any leads on this? It's blocking Pinterest from upgrading as well. I might be able to help but not sure where to start.

~~Adding `context` to  vendor `DllPlugin` solved it for me:~~

My comment was actually misleading DllPlugin context so it would bundle without making use of the vendor bundle (dll) that's why the error was gone.
Same error for me in v3.1.0 without the DLL plugin, but in case of CommonsChunkPlugin for a file inside the common chunck.

<s>What @enapupe suggested worked for the repo where I've managed to reproduce the error, thank you.

The fix was to add `context` to `webpack.DllPlugin`. Note that this is the part where you define the dll plugin, do not confuse it with `webpack.DllReferencePlugin`, the part where the dll is being referenced.</s>

What I've described does not work, it just masks the issue.

Why closed? Why context is required? 

> context (optional): context of requests in the manifest file (defaults to the webpack context.)

@enapupe If set context to DLL dist out dir, references to node_modules will be relative. Webpack simply ignores DLL in this case (because module not found). Are your sure that your solution is working and not just masks the issue ;)?
@develar I am sure the solution does NOT work for my case.
@develar @dexbol You are right, that option just made the DllPlugin to become useless. I'll edit my comment pointing that out. I don't have another solution.
Disabling ModuleConcatenationPlugin also doesn't help. DLL works only for some modules (e.g. works for vue, but doesn't work (=error is thrown) for vue-router).
@markogresak You should reconsider that `context` change. Check if your bundle is indeed not including vendor stuff (it should be).
